title: Card Flipping Game
summary: Given two arrays fronts and backs of length n, each representing the numbers on the front and back of n cards, determine the smallest number that can be made to face down on at least one card and not face up on any card by flipping any number of cards.
statement: Given two arrays fronts and backs of length n, each representing the numbers on the front and back of n cards, determine the smallest number that can be made to face down on at least one card and not face up on any card by flipping any number of cards. If no such number exists, return 0.
constraints: fronts and backs describe two sides of aligned cards.
After arbitrary flips, find the smallest front value absent from the back of every card showing it; return 0 if none.
hints: A value is impossible exactly when some card shows it on both sides.
Collect equal-side values as forbidden, then minimize all side values outside that set.
bad={front where front==back}; candidates=(fronts union backs)-bad.
Any allowed side value can be exposed by flipping its card, and forbidden values cannot be removed from their equal-sided card.
editorial: Any allowed side value can be exposed by flipping its card, and forbidden values cannot be removed from their equal-sided card.

tests.explanation: Values one and four are forbidden by equal-sided cards; two is the smallest remaining candidate.
The only value appears on both sides of its card and can never be made good.
